title: First-order improvement
labels: DETERMINISTIC FIXTURE EVALUATION — executable validators on synthetic change-review cases; no model was run

Both candidates were written by the same author who wrote the held-out cases. This shows the machinery separates a flawed candidate from a sound one; it is not evidence about a model's ability to generalize.

steps.claim: An observed failure is recorded with what actually went wrong
steps.observed: 13 verified failures in 40 reviews under release r1 (accuracy 68%): type_changed×3, field_removed×4, field_renamed×3, required_added×2, enum_value_removed×1

steps.claim: The first candidate is an executable change to a skill, judged on held-out cases against a frozen protocol
steps.observed: adds execution.json, validators/interface_compat.mjs; protocol frozen 2026-11-14T21:59:12.104Z; scored once on holdout-A

steps.claim: A candidate that helps but harms something else is rejected, and its result kept
steps.observed: accuracy 0.5 → 0.6, but Share of safe changes blocked: candidate 50.0%, incumbent 0.0%; allowed margin 5.0%.

steps.claim: A revision is never scored on cases its lineage has already seen results for
steps.observed: first attempt on holdout-A; revision on holdout-B; the first set is recorded as development data for this lineage

steps.claim: The revised candidate is compared with the incumbent and the fixed original baseline
Acceptance creates a release manifest but does not make it the default
steps.observed: r2: execution v2, coordination v1, evolution v1; rollback target r1; active release still r1

steps.claim: The qualified release is monitored in a bounded canary on fresh cases
A healthy canary is retained and applies to future work only
steps.observed: active release is now r2; r1 is retired and remains the rollback target

steps.claim: The evaluation ledger is complete and intact
steps.observed: 17 ledger entries, hash chain intact; protected store matches its sealed digest
